date_note: Euronews's article of 24 November reports the alert as issued on Tuesday (24 November); the page gives no earlier day.
title: UK NPSA and Ministry of Defence warn Ukraine-supply firms of Russian sabotage attempts, Euronews reports
org: National Protective Security Authority / Ministry of Defence
summary: Euronews reports that the UK's National Protective Security Authority and Ministry of Defence issued a joint alert to organisations supplying Ukraine's armed forces. The alert says Russia has increased attempts at sabotage against European defence-related facilities, using proxy actors and low-sophistication methods. Euronews also reports closed-door briefings for defence and critical national infrastructure CEOs on Tuesday and Wednesday.
plain: UK authorities have warned firms that supply Ukraine's military that Russia is trying more sabotage against European defence-related sites.
exec: Firms in the Ukraine supply chain are told by UK authorities, per Euronews, that they may be targets of Russian-linked sabotage.
action: The NPSA and MoD alert advises, as Euronews describes it, steps to reduce exposure to hostile reconnaissance, to detect and report suspicious activity, and to limit the impact of an attack.

validation.note: One publisher read: Euronews. The Daily Mail page could not be loaded and the NPSA/MoD alert itself was not found, so it was not read.
